companies.name: Alphabet
companies.one_line: Runs Google Cloud and Google DeepMind, and designs its own TPU chips.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.one_line: Runs AWS, a major investor in Anthropic, and designs its own AI chips.

companies.name: AMD
companies.one_line: Designs GPUs and CPUs for data centers; second GPU supplier to the large labs.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.one_line: Lab behind Claude, funded by hyperscalers and chipmakers that also sell it compute.

companies.name: Anysphere (Cursor)
companies.one_line: Maker of the Cursor coding app, a large customer of the AI labs.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.one_line: US maker of deposition, etch and inspection equipment for chip fabs.

companies.name: Arista
companies.one_line: US maker of data center network switches used by hyperscalers.

companies.name: Arm
companies.one_line: Licenses the CPU designs used across phones, servers and AI systems; controlled by SoftBank.

companies.name: ASML
companies.one_line: Dutch maker of chip lithography systems and the only supplier of EUV tools.

companies.name: Blackstone
companies.one_line: US alternative asset manager and a large owner of data centers through QTS.

companies.name: Blue Owl
companies.one_line: US alternative asset manager providing private credit and equity for data center campuses.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.one_line: Designs custom AI accelerators and networking chips for hyperscalers and labs.

companies.name: Brookfield
companies.one_line: Canadian alternative asset manager investing in power and data center infrastructure.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.one_line: US maker of optical components and transceivers that link AI servers together.

companies.name: Constellation
companies.one_line: US power producer with the largest US nuclear fleet, selling power to hyperscalers.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.one_line: US GPU cloud that rents Nvidia capacity to labs and hyperscalers, financed largely with debt.

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.one_line: US developer and operator of large AI data center campuses.

companies.name: Dell
companies.one_line: US maker of servers and PCs that sells AI server systems to labs, clouds and enterprises.

companies.name: Digital Realty
companies.one_line: US data center landlord that leases space and power to cloud providers.

companies.name: Foxconn (Hon Hai)
companies.one_line: Taiwanese electronics assembler and the largest builder of AI servers and racks.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.one_line: US maker of gas turbines and grid equipment; power for new data centers.

companies.name: Intel
companies.one_line: Designs and makes CPUs and runs a contract foundry business; has the US government and Nvidia as shareholders.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.one_line: US maker of etch and deposition equipment, with heavy exposure to memory makers.

companies.name: Lambda
companies.one_line: US GPU cloud selling AI compute to labs, hyperscalers and developers.

companies.name: Meta
companies.one_line: Spends at hyperscale on AI data centers for its own apps and models.

companies.name: MGX
companies.one_line: Abu Dhabi investment company focused on AI, investing in labs, data centers and Stargate.

companies.name: Micron
companies.one_line: US memory maker supplying high-bandwidth memory for AI chips.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.one_line: Runs Azure, the largest outside funder of OpenAI and an investor in Anthropic.

companies.name: Mistral
companies.one_line: French lab building open and commercial AI models.

companies.name: Nebius
companies.one_line: Amsterdam-based GPU cloud selling AI capacity to hyperscalers and model developers.

companies.name: Nvidia
companies.one_line: Designs the GPUs and networking at the core of most AI data centers, and invests across the chain.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.one_line: Lab behind ChatGPT and the largest buyer of compute across the chain.

companies.name: Oracle
companies.one_line: Runs Oracle Cloud and builds large compute capacity for OpenAI.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.one_line: Software company selling AI platforms to governments and enterprises.

companies.name: Perplexity
companies.one_line: AI search app that pays labs and clouds for model access and compute.

companies.name: Salesforce
companies.one_line: Enterprise software company selling AI agents and investing in AI startups.

companies.name: Samsung
companies.one_line: Korean maker of memory chips at scale, with a contract foundry business on the side.

companies.name: SK Hynix
companies.one_line: Korean memory maker and the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory for AI chips.

companies.name: SoftBank Group
companies.one_line: Japanese investment group, a major OpenAI backer, Stargate partner and owner of most of Arm.

companies.name: Stargate (JV)
companies.one_line: AI infrastructure venture announced by OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and MGX to build US data centers.

companies.name: Supermicro
companies.one_line: US maker of AI servers and rack systems, close to the GPU cloud providers.

companies.name: Tokyo Electron
companies.one_line: Japanese maker of chip fabrication equipment, strongest in coating, etch and deposition.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.one_line: Taiwanese contract chipmaker that fabricates and packages nearly every leading AI chip.

companies.name: US Government
companies.one_line: US federal government, which funds chipmakers through CHIPS Act grants and has taken equity stakes.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.one_line: US maker of power and cooling equipment for data centers.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.one_line: US power producer selling generation capacity to data center operators.

companies.name: xAI
companies.one_line: Lab behind Grok that builds and owns its own compute clusters.

deals.summary: Amazon invests $5B now and up to $20B more if business targets are met, on top of $8B invested earlier.
AMD grants Meta a warrant for up to 160M AMD shares, vesting as Meta's purchases scale to 6 GW and AMD hits share price thresholds.
Warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares, vesting with GPU deployments and AMD share-price targets. No dollar value stated.
Anthropic to spend more than $100B on AWS technologies over ten years.

deals.notes: Broadcom's CEO stated this on earnings calls; stored as reported because only press accounts of the calls are cited.
deals.summary: Anthropic orders $10B of TPU Ironwood racks from Broadcom; disclosed as an unnamed customer in September, named in December.

deals.notes: Separate order from the $10B one, so a separate edge. Stored as reported for the same reason.
deals.summary: Anthropic places a further $11B order with Broadcom for TPU racks.
Anthropic commits to buy $30B of Azure compute capacity.

deals.notes: Stated in euros only; no USD figure is stored because the source gives none.
deals.summary: ASML leads Mistral AI's Series C with EUR 1.3B for about 11% fully diluted, plus a long-term partnership.

deals.notes: Press reports put a dollar value on this deal; the company release does not, so none is stored.
deals.summary: Meta to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs, first gigawatt shipping in the second half of 2026. No dollar value stated.
Meta commits to a multiyear build on millions of NVIDIA Blackwell and Rubin GPUs, Grace CPUs and Spectrum-X networking. No dollar value stated.
Microsoft commits to invest up to $5B in Anthropic.
Five-year GPU capacity agreement worth about $17.4B through 2031, up to about $19.4B with extra services.
NVIDIA commits to invest up to $10B in Anthropic.

deals.notes: Amount and price are from Intel's 8-K. Closing in December 2025 is reported by The Register citing Intel filings.
deals.summary: NVIDIA buys $5B of Intel common stock at $23.28 a share alongside a product partnership.
NVIDIA intends to invest up to $100B in OpenAI, paid in step with each gigawatt deployed; letter of intent.
OpenAI to deploy 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs, first 1 GW in the second half of 2026. No dollar value stated.
OpenAI and Broadcom to deploy 10 GW of OpenAI-designed accelerator racks from late 2026 to end of 2029. No dollar value stated.

deals.notes: OpenAI projects demand of up to 900,000 DRAM wafers a month across suppliers; Samsung's share is not stated.
deals.summary: Samsung signs a letter of intent to supply DRAM to OpenAI's Stargate. No dollar value or volume share stated.
SK hynix signs a non-binding letter of intent to supply HBM to OpenAI's Stargate. Volumes and value to be set later.
SoftBank buys $2B of Intel common stock at $23 a share.

deals.notes: Funded by $5.7B of awarded but unpaid CHIPS grants plus $3.2B of Secure Enclave funds, so Intel's CHIPS grant is not a separate edge. Includes a five-year warrant for 5% more at $20 that applies only if Intel's foundry ownership drops below 51%. Announced date taken from the exhibit's file name. Closing not yet checked.
deals.summary: US government takes a 9.9% Intel stake: $8.9B for 433.3M shares at $20.47, funded by unpaid CHIPS grants and Secure Enclave money.

deals.notes: A separate preliminary award of up to $275M for Virginia was announced the same day and is not included. Amount disbursed is not tracked.
deals.summary: Final CHIPS award of up to $6.165B in direct funding for Micron's New York and Idaho fabs.

deals.notes: Paid against construction, production and commercial milestones. Amount disbursed is not tracked.
deals.summary: Final CHIPS award of up to $4.745B in direct funding for Samsung's Taylor and Austin, Texas fabs.

deals.notes: Up to $500M of loans also available and not counted.
deals.summary: Final CHIPS award of up to $458M in direct funding for SK hynix's AI memory packaging plant in Indiana.

deals.notes: Direct funding only; the loans are not counted. Paid against milestones; amount disbursed so far is not tracked.
deals.summary: Final CHIPS award of up to $6.6B in direct funding for TSMC's three Phoenix fabs, plus about $5B of loans available.
